scoring_notes: Computed truth is matched as a DIGIT RUN of the normalized text, never as a word (words.py): 'f(37)=896' carries 896, '1896' does not.
S5's truth and its C014 split read the WHOLE turn's speech, every pass, as the user hears it; the pass where the truth first appears is recorded.
S4's relay matches only the approval word(s) the KERNEL spoke in that run (the voice sink), and only while APPROVAL_WORDS_AR is byte-identical.
Where a structural signal and a word rule disagree (S8: spoke after the note without naming Docker), the run gets no side and its passage is read blind.
S4a's question is also put to the reader on the S4 passage, which is read for S4b anyway: a second opinion beside the word match, never replacing it.
Silence satisfies S1's A side, S1c's B side and S5's B side as well as K10's invisible side: a configuration silent on any must-speak pass has all four marked UNRELIABLE.

Padding: the A-against-A-prime pair is the calibration (its pooled S2 spread; allowance = the larger arm's flag count). A later configuration's explain rate is UNRELIABLE only when its flags exceed the allowance; in the pair itself it reads 'calibration'.
